Locked in: Friday 19 December 2025, 3–7 pm for the outdoor community picnic.

Based on your preferences (sea breeze, shade, nearby shelters, accessibility, toilets, 60–80 people, medium budget), here are good Darwin options:

1) Nightcliff Foreshore (around Nightcliff Jetty / picnic areas)
- Why it fits: Strong sea breeze, shaded grass areas, coastal views. Multiple picnic shelters and gas BBQs along the foreshore, generally flat and accessible paths.
- Pros: Classic community vibe, good sunset aspect, toilets and parking along the foreshore, easy to split into food / games zones.
- Watchouts: Popular on Friday afternoons; to be safe you’d enquire with council about booking specific shelters. Breeze can be strong, so secure tablecloths/signage.

2) East Point Reserve
- Why it fits: Large lawns with tree shade and regular sea breeze, several picnic areas with shelters and BBQs, shared paths that are suitable for prams/mobility devices.
- Pros: Lots of space for kids’ games away from traffic, easier to “buffer” your group from others, toilets and parking nearby.
- Watchouts: Some areas are more exposed; best to pick a tree-lined or shelter-adjacent spot and share a simple map so people find you.

3) Botanic Gardens side near Mindil (George Brown Darwin Botanic Gardens)
- Why it fits: Shaded lawns, some shelters, accessible paths, toilets; you still get airflow without being fully exposed on the beach.
- Pros: Family‑friendly, good for older attendees (shade, flat paths), your small battery speaker at low volume is usually fine.
- Watchouts: Check for other events; parking can be busier if something else is on.

Draft run-sheet for 19 Dec (3–7 pm)

- 2:00–3:00 pm – Setup
  - Setup crew arrives, claims shelter/lawn area.
  - Set up tables, rugs/chairs, BBQ area, kids’ games zone, welcome/sign-in table, and battery speaker.

- 3:00–3:30 pm – Arrival
  - Welcome table with sign-in and basic info.
  - Drinks and light snacks available.

- 3:30–5:00 pm – Main picnic + BBQ
  - Gas BBQ running; potluck dishes laid out.
  - Informal kids’ games (balls, frisbees, simple races, bubbles, colouring).
  - Background music at low volume.

- 5:00–6:30 pm – Community activities & social time
  - Short welcome/acknowledgement, group photo.
  - Optional simple group activity (quiz, scavenger hunt, or kids’ relay).
  - Continue food and mingling.

- 6:30–7:00 pm – Pack‑up
  - Collect rubbish, pack food and gear, check area is clean.
  - Final thanks/announcements.

Key logistics checklist (high-level)

Space & permissions
- Confirm chosen location and specific area (with map pin).
- Check if a council booking/permit is needed for:
  - Event size (60–80 people).
  - Use of particular shelter/BBQ.
  - Use of a battery speaker.

Equipment
- Seating/shade: rugs, some folding tables, optional extra shade (if allowed), camp chairs or BYO chairs.
- Food service: coolers/eskies and ice, serving tongs/utensils, chopping boards, plates/cups/napkins, rubbish and recycling bags.
- BBQ: access to gas BBQs or bring portable gas BBQ(s) plus a spare gas bottle.
- Activities: balls, frisbees, cones, chalk, bubbles, simple prizes, colouring supplies.
- Audio/signage: battery speaker, basic playlist, simple signs (“Picnic here”, arrows from car park).

Food & drink
- BBQ items (sausages, veg options, bread, onions, sauces).
- Potluck sign‑up (salads / mains / desserts / snacks).
- Water (large jugs or refill station) plus soft drinks/juice; encourage BYO bottles.
- Food safety: keep perishables in eskies; hand sanitiser at food and games tables; shade over food.

Accessibility & comfort
- Check shortest flat route from parking to your area.
- Confirm toilets within a short walk.
- Provide at least one quieter/shady “rest” spot.
- Basic first‑aid kit on site, plus sunblock and insect repellent at the welcome table.

Light rain plan
- Choose a spot adjacent to a solid shelter.
- If a brief shower hits, move food and people under shelter, pause BBQ if needed.
- Decide one communication channel (e.g., SMS list or social post) for last‑minute updates.

Next step:
1) Which location would you like to use: Nightcliff Foreshore, East Point Reserve, or the Botanic Gardens area?  
2) Once you choose, do you want a more detailed checklist with suggested quantities (e.g., how many tables, sausages, drinks) and a simple roles list for volunteers?</action>

<action type="say">
Great choice—Nightcliff Foreshore near the jetty is ideal for breeze and views.

Below is a detailed, practical plan for ~70 people (mid‑point of 60–80). Adjust up/down if your RSVPs change.

1) Equipment & setup checklist (Nightcliff Foreshore, jetty area)

Shelter & seating
- Ground cover:
  - 6–8 large picnic rugs/ground sheets.
- Tables:
  - 4–6 folding trestle tables (2–3 for food/drink, 1–2 for sign‑in/activities).
- Chairs:
  - 20–30 folding chairs (plus encourage BYO chairs).
- Shade:
  - Rely mainly on existing shelter/trees.
  - Optional: 1–2 small pop‑up gazebos if permitted and wind allows (check council and be ready to secure them very well).

Food service & BBQ
- BBQ:
  - 2–3 gas BBQ hotplates in use (existing council BBQs if available) OR 2 portable gas BBQs.
  - Gas: 2 full gas bottles if bringing your own, plus 1 spare if possible.
- Cooking gear:
  - 6–8 BBQ tongs/spatulas.
  - 2–3 chopping boards.
  - 3–4 sharp knives (kept at food table, not kids’ area).
  - Aluminium trays / roasting pans for cooked food: 6–8.
- Serving:
  - 6–8 serving spoons/tongs.
  - 4–6 large bowls/trays (for salads, chips).
  - 2–3 jugs for water/juice.

Tables & hygiene
- Plates: ~100 (mix of reusable or sturdy compostable).
- Cups: ~120.
- Napkins/serviettes: ~300.
- Cutlery:
  - Forks ~100, knives ~80, spoons ~80 (less if mostly finger food/BBQ).
- Hygiene:
  - 3–4 large pump bottles of hand sanitiser (BBQ, food table, games zone).
  - 2 rolls of paper towel.
  - 1 basic first‑aid kit.
  - 2–3 bottles of sunscreen, 2–3 bottles of insect repellent.

Cold storage & rubbish
- Eskies/coolers:
  - 4–6 large eskies (2–3 for drinks, 2–3 for perishables).
- Ice:
  - ~6–8 large bags of ice (more if very hot).
- Rubbish:
  - 6–8 large garbage bags.
  - 3–4 recycling bags/boxes (for cans/bottles).
  - 3–4 portable bins/buckets or boxes to line with bags.
- Cleaning:
  - Dish tub + sponge/cloths + small dish soap (for reusable items).
  - Wipes for tables.

Activities & signage
- Kids’ games:
  - 2–3 balls, 2–3 frisbees.
  - 10–12 cones or markers for simple games.
  - Chalk (if on paths near you is appropriate).
  - Bubbles (4–6 bottles).
  - Simple prizes (20–30 small items).
  - Colouring: 30–40 printed sheets, 2–3 sets of pencils/crayons.
- Signage:
  - 4–6 A4/A3 signs (e.g., “Community Picnic →”, “Food”, “Kids’ Games”, “Welcome/Info”).
  - Tape, blu‑tack, or cable ties for attaching signs.
- Audio:
  - 1 small battery speaker, fully charged + backup power bank if needed.
  - Pre‑made playlist on a phone; ensure it’s easy to keep volume low.

Comfort & safety
- Lighting (if it gets dim by 7 pm):
  - 2–3 battery lanterns or fairy lights (optional, but handy).
- Weather:
  - A few tarps or extra plastic tablecloths to quickly cover food tables if showers pass through.
- Misc:
  - Clipboards and pens (3–4) for sign‑in lists, games, notes.

2) Food & drink quantities (for ~70 people)

Assuming mix of BBQ + potluck. These are the “host‑provided” baselines; potluck dishes reduce how much you must buy.

BBQ items (host‑supplied)
- Sausages:
  - 1.5–2 per person → ~110–140 sausages.
- Veggie options:
  - Veggie sausages/burgers: enough for at least 15–20 people (even if fewer are vegetarian) → ~25–30 veggie items.
- Bread:
  - 6–8 loaves of sliced bread, OR 80–90 long rolls.
- Onions:
  - 4–5 kg (pre‑slice if possible).
- Sauces:
  - Tomato sauce x 2 large bottles.
  - BBQ sauce x 2 large bottles.
  - Mustard x 1 bottle.
  - Possibly 1–2 squeezy bottles of mayo.
- Extras:
  - 3–4 bottles of mixed condiments (pickles, relish).
  - 2–3 large bags of grated cheese (optional).

Potluck guidance (for your sign‑up sheet)
- Ask attendees to bring:
  - Salads: aim for 8–10 large salad bowls.
  - Snacks: 6–8 large bags of chips/crisps + dips.
  - Desserts: 6–8 cakes/slices/fruit platters.

Drinks
- Water:
  - Plan for at least 2–3 litres per 10 people → ~15–20 litres total.
  - Large dispensers or refillable jugs + encourage BYO bottles.
- Soft drinks/juice:
  - 1–1.5 standard cans/serves per person → 70–100 serves total (mix of cans and juice).
- Ice:
  - As above, ~6–8 bags (more if you expect people to bring extra drinks).

3) Simple volunteer roles list

Aim for about 14–18 volunteers across roles (people can do more than one role in shifts).

Coordination
- Event coordinator (1)
  - Overall contact; liaises with council if needed, oversees run‑sheet, handles issues.
- Setup/pack‑up lead (1)
  - Organises who arrives early / stays late; ensures space is left clean.

Setup & pack‑up
- Setup crew (4–6)
  - Arrive 2–2:30 pm.
  - Claim shelter/space, set up tables, rugs, signage, games area, food/drinks stations.
- Pack‑up crew (4–6; can overlap with setup crew)
  - From ~6:30 pm.
  - Collect rubbish, check BBQs, pack equipment, final sweep of area.

Food & BBQ
- BBQ team (3–4)
  - Manage raw vs cooked separation and food safety.
  - Cook sausages/veggie options steadily across 3:30–6 pm.
- Food table team (2–3)
  - Arrange potluck dishes, keep serving area tidy, monitor stock of plates/cups/napkins, keep food shaded and covered.

Welcome & info
- Welcome/registration (2)
  - At a small “Welcome” table near access path.
  - Greet people, answer “where’s…?” questions, point to food, toilets, kids’ area.
  - Optionally collect names/emails or mark attendance.

  - Gas: 2 full gas bottles if bringing your own, plus 1 spare if possible.
- Cooking gear:
  - 6–8 BBQ tongs/spatulas.
  - 2–3 chopping boards.
  - 3–4 sharp knives (kept at food table, not kids’ area).
  - Aluminium trays / roasting pans for cooked food: 6–8.
- Serving:
  - 6–8 serving spoons/tongs.
  - 4–6 large bowls/trays (for salads, chips).
  - 2–3 jugs for water/juice.

Tables & hygiene
- Plates: ~100 (mix of reusable or sturdy compostable).
- Cups: ~120.
- Napkins/serviettes: ~300.
- Cutlery:
  - Forks ~100, knives ~80, spoons ~80 (less if mostly finger food/BBQ).
- Hygiene:
  - 3–4 large pump bottles of hand sanitiser (BBQ, food table, games zone).
  - 2 rolls of paper towel.
  - 1 basic first‑aid kit.
  - 2–3 bottles of sunscreen, 2–3 bottles of insect repellent.

- Ice:
  - ~6–8 large bags of ice (more if very hot).
- Rubbish:
  - 6–8 large garbage bags.
  - 3–4 recycling bags/boxes (for cans/bottles).
  - 3–4 portable bins/buckets or boxes to line with bags.
